management.commentary: CEO Dr. Chih-Hsiang (Thompson) Lin (founder, since 1997) and CFO Dr. Stefan Murry raised 2026 revenue guidance to >$1.1B (from >$1B) and operating income to >$140M after Q1 record $151M (+51% YoY), citing customer demand for 800G/1.6T outstripping production through mid-2027.[3][4] Gross margin target lifts toward ~40% long-term as the 800G/1.6T mix scales.[3]

bull_case: 2026 revenue guide raised to **>$1.1B** (from >$1B), ~2.4× FY25's $456M — execution against $324M+ order backlog now underway.[3][4]
**800G shipments start Q2 2026**, scaling to **500K+ units/month combined 800G/1.6T by YE2026**; 1.6T in Q3 ramping to full Q4. Texas Sugar Land 210K sq-ft facility ramps mid-to-late 2026.[3][6]
Confirmed **$124M in 800G** + **$200M+ in 1.6T** from a major hyperscale customer; customer demand outstripping production capacity through mid-2027.[1][2]
Rosenblatt raised PT from **$140 → $220** (Buy) on May 8, citing Amazon 800G strength + upcoming Oracle qualifications. Street raising PTs post-print.[5]
Stacked-bullish MA structure (MA20 $174 > MA50 $142 > MA200 $63), RSI 54.9 (room above), 76% through 52W range with consolidation under recent $233.67 high — textbook pullback in uptrend.
Cash $440M, current ratio 3.83×, D/E 0.25× — financial flexibility to fund Texas capex without dilution risk.
Gross margin targeting **~40% long-term** as 800G/1.6T mix scales (currently 29.6%); operating leverage as scale ramps — guide for **$140M+ FY26 op income**.[3]
bear_case: Consensus avg PT $82.80 (broad analyst aggregate) implies ~54% downside from $181 spot; PT dispersion from $25 to $220 unusually wide — analysts disagree sharply on out-year execution.
Fwd P/S **28.7×** and Fwd P/E **38×** — priced for flawless execution; any production slip in Sugar Land ramp or 1.6T qualification delay = sharp multiple compression.
FY25 operating margin **-8.6%** and FCF **-$446M**; still unprofitable on GAAP basis. Profitability not expected until H2 2026 — execution risk if 1.6T ramp slips.
Heavy **customer concentration**: a single hyperscale customer drives the bulk of the 800G/1.6T narrative. Order timing risk + pricing power risk if that customer dual-sources.
Latest Q1 EPS -$0.07 missed -$0.048 estimate (**-45% surprise**) — short-term execution wobble despite revenue beat.[4]
ATR(14) of **$25.35 = ~14% of price** — wide intraday range means stops must be loose and position sizing has to scale down; whipsaw + drawdown risk are real.
Competitive pressure from LITE, MRVL, COHR also scaling 800G transceivers; AAOI's lead is execution, not technology moat.

trade_plan_long.name: Pullback Continuation in Uptrend
trade_plan_long.trigger: Reclaim and hold above $185 with volume; ideal entry on pullback to MA20 ($170-178) or retest of $160-165 pivot zone with bullish reversal.
trade_plan_long.stop: $155 (below 5d-low $160 and 10d-low $150.54 cluster; ~1× ATR below mid-entry — gives the trade ATR room)
targets: T1: $215 (measured move from MA50 base + breakout extension)
T3: $260+ (Rosenblatt $220 was pre-print; expect raises post Q2 if 800G ramp confirms)
trade_plan_long.rr_note: R:R from $175 entry, $155 stop, $233 target ≈ 2.9:1; to $215 ≈ 2:1. Use scale-in to improve effective R:R.
trade_plan_long.sizing_note: ATR-based: 1R = $25/share (1×ATR). User's R = $2,500 → 100 shares per $1R risk, ~$17,500 nominal at $175 entry (~1.75% of $1M equity). With 14% ATR, this is intentionally smaller than your default 5-10% position — wide stop demands smaller size to keep risk at 1R.

trade_plan_short.sizing_note: Short borrow on AAOI may be expensive given the rally — consider **June/Sept 160/120 put spreads** to define risk and avoid borrow cost. Spread max risk ~$5-10/contract, defined T1 target ~$15-20 mid.

ai_synthesis.earnings_risk_note: Next ER **2026-08-07** AMC (Q2). Options-implied move ±**13.2%** (~$24 on $181). Average of last 4 post-earnings moves trends similar. ATR(14) of $25 means a normal session already moves ~10%, so use wider mental stops, ATR-based sizing, and consider trimming half the position or hedging with put spreads into the print. Q1 EPS missed (-45% surprise) despite revenue beat — EPS variance is real.
catalysts: **May 8, 2026**: Rosenblatt raised PT from $140 to $220 (maintained Buy), citing Amazon 800G revenue strength + upcoming Oracle qualifications + raised 2026/long-term guidance.[5]
**May 7, 2026**: Q1 record revenue $151.1M (+51% YoY, +13% QoQ); EPS -$0.07 (slightly missed -$0.048 est); raised FY26 guide to >$1.1B (from >$1B), op income >$140M; Q2 guide $180-$198M.[3][4]
**Apr 24, 2026**: U.S. expansion accelerates — Texas Sugar Land 210K sq-ft facility on track to scale mid-to-late 2026; target 500K+ units/month combined 800G/1.6T by YE2026.[6]
**Apr 4, 2026**: Additional $71M in 800G single-mode orders disclosed from same major hyperscale customer (cumulative $124M since mid-March).[2]
**Mar 9, 2026**: First volume order for 1.6T transceivers from a major hyperscale customer totaling >$200M; shipments early Q3, completing Q4 2026.[1]
**CATV upside**: FY26 CATV revenue now expected at $325M+ vs prior guidance; amplifier demand tracking above expectations.[4]
**Q1 2026**: Tariff refund of $5.7M+ approved tied to overturned IEEPA tariffs.[3]
